UP1.claim: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India.

evidence.quote: It is the most populous state in India

UP2.claim: Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh.

evidence.quote: Lucknow is the state capital

UP3.claim: Uttar Pradesh recorded the most domestic tourist visits of any state in 2024: 646.81 million, 21.94% of the national total.

evidence.quote: For domestic tourist visits, the top five States were Uttar Pradesh (646.81 million; 21.94%)

UP4.claim: Uttar Pradesh recorded 2.27 million foreign tourist visits in 2024 (10.83% of the national total).

evidence.quote: Uttar Pradesh (2.27 million; 10.83%)

evidence.quote: It has three world heritage sites i.e. Taj Mahal, Agra Fort & Fatehpur Sikri

UP6.claim: The Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, in Varanasi, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in July 2026.

evidence.quote: The Ancient Buddhist Site, Sarnath, in Uttar Pradesh, India, has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List during the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee

UP7.claim: The Taj Mahal was India's most visited ticketed ASI monument in 2024–25, for both domestic (6.26 million) and foreign (0.65 million) visitors.

evidence.quote: Taj Mahal, Agra (6.26 million) was the most visited monument in 2024 for domestic visitors
In respect of foreign visitors, Taj Mahal, Agra (0.65 million) was the most visited monument in 2024

RJ1.claim: Rajasthan is India's largest state by area.

evidence.quote: It is the largest Indian state by area and the seventh largest by population .

RJ2.claim: Rajasthan was formed on 30 March 1949 from the merger of 22 kingdoms and principalities.

evidence.quote: Formed on March 30, 1949, it resulted from the merger of 22 kingdoms and principalities.

RJ3.claim: Rajasthan recorded 230.08 million domestic and 2.07 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, fifth among states for both.

evidence.quote: Rajasthan (230.08 million; 7.80%)
Rajasthan (2.07 million; 9.90%)

RJ4.claim: Rajasthan's cities are known by colour: Jodhpur the blue city, Jaipur the pink city, Udaipur the white city and Jaisalmer the golden city.

evidence.quote: Rajasthan's cities follow a colour code: Jodhpur is the blue city, Jaipur is the pink city, Udaipur is the white city, and Jaisalmer is the golden city.

RJ5.claim: Six hill forts — Amber, Chittor, Gagron, Jaisalmer, Kumbhalgarh and Ranthambore — became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013.

evidence.quote: Six forts of Rajasthan, namely, Amber Fort, Chittor Fort , Gagron Fort , Jaisalmer Fort , Kumbhalgarh and Ranthambore Fort were included in the UNESCO World Heritage Site list during the 37th meeting of the World Heritage Committee in Phnom Penh during June 2013.

RJ6.claim: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, stretches across Rajasthan.

evidence.quote: The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, stretches across Rajasthan

RJ7.claim: Keoladeo National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for birdwatchers, and Ranthambore is known for tigers.

evidence.quote: a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a haven for birdwatchers
Ranthambore is famous for its tiger population

MH1.claim: Maharashtra recorded 3.70 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, the most of any state.

evidence.quote: In the case of foreign tourist visits, the leading States were Maharashtra (3.70 million; 17.69%)

MH2.topic: Rock-cut caves and Mumbai's World Heritage Sites
MH2.claim: Maharashtra's World Heritage Sites include the Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta caves, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and Mumbai's Victorian Gothic and Art Deco ensembles.

evidence.quote: From the renowned Ajanta , Elephanta and Ellora Caves , showcasing ancient rock-cut architecture and exquisite cave art, to the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai

MH3.claim: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj founded the Maratha Empire in Maharashtra in the 17th century.

evidence.quote: Maharashtra is the land where the great Maratha warrior, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, founded the Maratha Empire in the 17th century

MH4.claim: The state runs from the Konkan coast to the Sahyadri (Western Ghats) ranges, with beaches such as Ganpatipule and Alibaug and treks such as Harishchandragad.

evidence.quote: From the serene Konkan coast to the rugged landscapes of the Western Ghats
You can also trek to Harishchandragad

MH5.claim: Ganesh Chaturthi is celebrated across the state and ends with the immersion of Ganesha idols in rivers and the sea.

evidence.quote: The festival culminates with the immersion of the idols in water bodies like rivers or the sea, amidst much fanfare and music.

MH6.claim: Signature foods include vada pav, misal pav, puran poli and modak.

evidence.quote: Savor the spicy Vada Pav on the bustling streets of Mumbai
The state's desserts, including the famous Puran Poli and Modak, are a must-try for anyone with a sweet tooth.

TN1.claim: Tamil Nadu recorded 306.8 million domestic and 1.16 million foreign tourist visits in 2024.

TN2.claim: Tamil Nadu's UNESCO sites include the Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram, the Great Living Chola Temples and the Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

evidence.quote: The state proudly boasts some of the finest UNESCO World Heritage sites namely the Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram, and the Great Living Chola Temples, apart from the Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

TN3.claim: Carnatic music and Bharatanatyam dance are central to Tamil culture.

evidence.quote: Carnatic music, cherished by the cultural elite for its intricate melodies, represents a significant aspect of the region's musical heritage.

TN4.claim: Tamil meals centre on rice and lentils and are traditionally served on a banana leaf, with sambar and coconut chutney.

evidence.quote: The traditional practice of serving meals on banana leaves adds a cultural touch to the dining experience.
Sambhar and Coconut Chutney, quintessential accompaniments to various dishes

TN5.claim: Pongal is Tamil Nadu's harvest festival.

evidence.quote: Pongal, the Harvest festival of state, marks a significant celebration.

BH1.claim: Bihar is the birthplace of Buddhism and Jainism.

evidence.quote: Bihar proudly stands as the birthplace of two major world religions, Buddhism and Jainism .

BH2.claim: Bihar recorded 0.737 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, up 35% on 2023.

BH3.claim: Chhath, dedicated to the Sun God, is Bihar's signature festival, usually between late October and mid-November.

evidence.quote: typically falling between late October and mid-November, spanning a celebration of up to four days

BH4.claim: Madhubani painting, made by women of the Mithila region with natural colours, is Bihar's best-known art.

evidence.quote: Among Bihar's artistic traditions, the works of Madhubani artists stand out.

BH5.claim: Bihar's name comes from 'vihara', a Buddhist monastery.

evidence.quote: derives its name from the Sanskrit and Pali word 'Vihara,' meaning dwelling place

BH6.claim: Patna, Bihar's capital, was originally called Pataliputra; Takhat Sri Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib marks the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh.

evidence.quote: Patna , the present-day capital of Bihar, was originally called Patliputra
it is the birthplace of the tenth Sikh Guru, Shri Guru Gobind Singh Ji Maharaj.

PB1.claim: Punjab recorded 27.7 million domestic and 0.54 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, both down on 2023.

PB2.claim: Amritsar's Golden Temple is the spiritual centre of Sikhism, famed for its langar.

evidence.quote: Don’t miss the community meals served here, known as ‘langar’.

PB3.claim: Virasat-e-Khalsa in Anandpur Sahib tells the story of the Sikh community; the town also hosts Hola Mohalla, a martial-arts and cultural festival.

evidence.quote: Head to Virasat-e-Khalsa in Anandpur Sahib that narrates the history and culture of the Sikh community.
the Hola Mohalla celebration, a grand martial arts and cultural festival

PB4.claim: Patiala's Qila Mubarak is a grand fort complex with museums of Punjab's royal past.

evidence.quote: In the historic city of Patiala stands the grand Qila Mubarak

PB5.claim: Harike Wetland, at the confluence of the Beas and Sutlej, is the largest wetland in northern India and a birdwatching haven.

evidence.quote: Located at the confluence of the Beas and Sutlej rivers, Harike Wetland and Bird Sanctuary
Birdwatchers will be delighted by the avian diversity at the largest wetland in northern India.

PB6.claim: Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar recalls the 1919 massacre.

evidence.quote: pay a visit to the Jallianwala Bagh, a sombre reminder of India's struggle for independence, that bears witness to the tragic massacre of 1919.

PB7.claim: Kapurthala's Sheesh Mahal is a palace of mirrorwork inspired by Versailles.

evidence.quote: a dazzling palace adorned with intricate mirrorwork inspired by the Palace of Versailles.

WB1.claim: West Bengal recorded 184.5 million domestic and 3.12 million foreign tourist visits in 2024 — second among states for foreign visits.

evidence.quote: West Bengal (3.12 million; 14.92%)

WB2.claim: Kolkata, the state capital, is known as India's cultural capital; its Indian Museum was founded in 1814.

evidence.quote: This vibrant state, home to the cultural capital of India, Kolkata
Kolkata is home to India's oldest and largest museum, the Indian Museum , founded in 1814

WB3.claim: Durga Puja, celebrated over nine days with elaborate pandals, is the state's grandest festival.

evidence.quote: Durga Puja reigning as the region's most beloved celebration
spans nine days

evidence.quote: The Sunderbans, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, showcases the unique coexistence of man and nature.

WB5.claim: Highlights include Bishnupur's terracotta temples and Kolkata's Victoria Memorial.

evidence.quote: From the majestic terracotta temples of Bishnupur, adorned with intricate sculptures, to the iconic Victoria Memorial in Kolkata

WB7.claim: In the north, the tea gardens of Darjeeling are a major draw.

evidence.quote: For nature enthusiasts, the lush tea gardens of Darjeeling and the dense mangrove forests of the Sundarbans

WB6.claim: Bengal is famous for sweets such as rasogolla, sandesh and rasamalai, and for fish dishes including hilsa.

The diversity of fish available, ranging from prawns to hilsa (ilish mach)

JK1.claim: Jammu and Kashmir recorded 23.0 million domestic and 0.065 million foreign tourist visits in 2024.

JK2.claim: Pilgrims come for the Amarnath cave and the Vaishno Devi Temple.

evidence.quote: The revered Hindu pilgrimage, Amarnath, dedicated to Lord Shiva and Vaishno Devi Temple dedicated to goddess Shakti draw countless devotees from all over the country.

JK3.claim: The Dal and Nigeen lakes are known for houseboat stays; spring brings tulips.

evidence.quote: The Karewa lake, Dal Lake, and Nageen Lakes, each exude their own distinct charm
The arrival of spring heralds the vibrant blossoms of tulips

JK4.claim: Jammu's dishes include khatta meat, madra (kidney beans in yoghurt) and khameera bread.

evidence.quote: Try Khameera, a delectable local bread
For non-vegetarians there are a variety of dishes including Khatta Meat

JK_ADV.topic: UK travel advice: against all travel
JK_ADV.claim: As of October 2026, the UK government advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir, including Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg, except air travel to and within the city of Jammu.

evidence.quote: FCDO advises against all travel to the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir (including Pahalgam, Gulmarg, Sonamarg, the city of Srinagar and the Jammu-Srinagar national highway)
Still current at: 27 October 2026

JK_ATK.claim: On 22 April 2025, militants killed 26 civilians, most of them tourists, near Pahalgam.

evidence.quote: in which 26 civilians were killed on 22 April 2025

UP8.claim: Awadhi and Mughal cuisines lead in Uttar Pradesh — dum biryani, dum gosht and nihari — and Agra is the home of petha.

evidence.quote: Uttar Pradesh boasts a rich culinary heritage, with Awadhi and Mughal cuisines taking centre stage, particularly celebrated in Lucknow.
Notable dishes include Dum Biryani, Dum Gosht, and Nihari
Petha, a renowned sweet delicacy, finds its origin in the city of Agra.

UP9.claim: Uttar Pradesh is known for Lucknow's chikankari, Varanasi zari, Moradabad metalwork, and Khurja and Chunar pottery.

evidence.quote: Chikankari, a delicate and traditional hand embroidery craft, represents a vital facet of Uttar Pradesh's artistic heritage, predominantly practiced in Lucknow.
Varanasi's Zari work being renowned globally
Moradabad stands out for its art metalwork
In the world of pottery, Khurja, Chunar, and Rampur take the lead

UP10.claim: Mathura and Vrindavan, Ayodhya and Varanasi are the state's great pilgrimage centres; Sarnath, Kushinagar, Kapilvastu and Sravasti are sacred to Buddhists.

evidence.quote: Visiting Mathura and Vrindavan brings travellers closer to a land adorned with magnificent temples dedicated to Lord Krishna
Ayodhya, renowned as the birthplace of Lord Ram, stands as another prime spiritual destination in Uttar Pradesh
These include Sarnath , Vindhyachal, Kushinagar, Kapilvastu, and Sravasti

UP11.claim: Lucknow, the city of Nawabs, has historic monuments and palaces.

evidence.quote: The city of Nawabs, Lucknow, reveals a unique blend of ancient and modern, boasting historic monuments, forts, and palaces

UP12.claim: Varanasi is known for Bharat Milap and Chhath, and Prayagraj for the Kumbh, Magh and Ardh Kumbh melas.

evidence.quote: Varanasi, for instance, is renowned for Bharat Milap and Chhath Pooja
Prayagraj is particularly famous for Kumbh Mela – world’s largest gathering of humans, Magh Mela, and Ardha Mela

UP13.claim: In summer, hot winds called loo blow across Uttar Pradesh.

evidence.quote: In summer, hot winds called loo blow all across Uttar Pradesh.

UP14.claim: The south-west monsoon brings most of the state's rain after summer.

evidence.quote: After summer it is the southwest monsoon which brings most of the rain here

UP15.claim: Lucknow has cool, dry winters from late November to February and hot summers from late March to early June.

evidence.quote: Lucknow has a humid subtropical climate ( Köppen Cwa ) with cool, dry winters from late November to February and dry, hot summers with sunshine from late March to early June.

UP16.claim: October to March is the pleasant season in Mathura.

evidence.quote: Plan your visit between October and March, when pleasant weather graces the city.

UP17.claim: The main airports are Lucknow (14 km from the city), Varanasi (22 km) and Ayodhya (about 10 km from Ayodhya Dham).

evidence.quote: Situated in Amausi, 14 kilometers from the city’s nucleus
LBS airport Babatpur which is 22 km. from Varanasi
Maharishi Valmiki International Airport Ayodhya which is approximately 10km from Ayodhya Dham

UP18.claim: The Agra and Purvanchal expressways connect Lucknow with Agra and eastern UP.

evidence.quote: The majestic Agra Expressway and Purvanchal Expressway serve as lifelines, bridging Lucknow to the nation’s sprawling urban landscape.

UP19.claim: Prayagraj's Magh Mela is held every year from mid-January to mid-February.

evidence.quote: This Mela is held every year during the Hindu month of Magh (corresponding from mid January – mid February)

UP20.claim: Barsana's Lathmar Holi falls in February or March.

evidence.quote: In the months of February or March, the people of Barsana celebrate the renowned Lathmar Holi.

UP21.claim: Autumn is the best season to visit Varanasi.

evidence.quote: Autumn is the best season to visit Varanasi

RJS1.claim: Winter, from about October to January, is the best time to visit Rajasthan, with temperatures of roughly 10–30°C in most parts.

evidence.quote: Winters  – The winters are marked as being the best season to visit Rajasthan.
the princely state enjoys a mild weather with temperatures ranging between 10°C – 30°C for most parts
Winters in Rajasthan usually commence around October and extend to January.

RJS2.claim: The Jaipur Literature Festival, Udaipur World Music Festival and Pushkar Fair all fall in the winter season.

evidence.quote: including the Jaipur Literature Festival, Udaipur World Music Festival, Camel Fair, and Pushkar Fair, are observed during the winter season

RJS3.claim: Summers are hot and dry, with temperatures up to 48°C; Mount Abu, Ranakpur and Kumbhalgarh are pleasant in summer.

evidence.quote: Summers in Rajasthan are usually hot and dry, with temperatures rising up to as high as 48 degrees Celsius.
summers in places like Mount Abu, Ranakpur, and Kumbhalgarh in Rajasthan, which are the places to which tourists mostly flock to when visiting the state in this season, are rather pleasant

RJS4.claim: In the monsoon, Rajasthan turns green and celebrates the Teej festival.

evidence.quote: Visiting Rajasthan during the monsoon season, you will be welcomed by lush greenery, rainbows, and peacocks dancing around.
as various parts of the state ready up for the Teej festival in the monsoon season

RJS5.claim: Rajasthan's three major airports are Jaipur (domestic and international), Jodhpur and Udaipur (domestic).

evidence.quote: The three major airports of Rajasthan are Sanganer International Airport in Jaipur, Jodhpur Airport and Dabok Airport in Udaipur.
While Sanganer is open to domestic and international air traffic, Jodhpur and Udaipur only serve domestic routes

RJS6.claim: Jaipur and Kota are the main rail hubs; Udaipur, Jodhpur, Ajmer, Bikaner and Abu Road are other major stations.

evidence.quote: The major railway stations of Rajasthan are Jaipur, Kota, Bharatpur, Bikaner, Ajmer, Alwar, Udaipur, Abu Road and Jodhpur.
But out of this lot, Jaipur and Kota are major hubs connecting the major cities of India to Rajasthan.

RJS7.claim: NH-8 between Delhi and Mumbai runs through Jaipur, Ajmer, Udaipur and Chittorgarh; RSRTC runs state buses.

evidence.quote: The NH-8 which connects Mumbai to Delhi is the busiest national highway in Rajasthan and runs through Ajmer, Jaipur, Udaipur and Chittorgarh.
hop onto a bus operated by the Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation

RJS8.claim: The Hill Forts of Rajasthan — Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore (Sawai Madhopur), Gagron (Jhalawar), Amber (Jaipur) and Jaisalmer — became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013.

evidence.quote: The serial site, situated in the state of Rajastahan, includes six majestic forts in Chittorgarh; Kumbhalgarh; Sawai Madhopur; Jhalawar; Jaipur, and Jaisalmer.
They have been clustered as a series and designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013.

RJS9.claim: The Pushkar Fair is a week-long camel and livestock fair held between October and November, one of the world's largest.

evidence.quote: is an annual weeklong camel and livestock fair held in the town of Pushkar between the months of October and November
It is one of the world's largest camel

RJS10.claim: The Desert Festival, with camel races, camel polo and folk dances, is held around January–February.

evidence.quote: Organised by the Department of Tourism around January-February, the Desert Festival is the best place to enjoy rich and colourful Rajasthani folk culture.
The high points of the festival are puppeteers, acrobats, camel races, camel polo, folk dances, etc.

RJS11.claim: Udaipur, the 'Venice of the East', is a city of lakes ringed by the green Aravalli hills; the Lake Palace stands in the middle of Lake Pichola.

evidence.quote: Often referred to as the 'Venice of the East', the city of lakes Udaipur is located around azure water lakes and is hemmed in by lush green hills of Aravallis.
The famous Lake Palace, located in the middle of Lake Pichola is one of the most beautiful sights of Udaipur.

RJS12.claim: Jaisalmer, the 'Golden City', sits near the Pakistan border on the edge of the Thar Desert; its landmark is the Sonar Qila.

evidence.quote: This 'Golden City’ is located close to the Pakistan border and in close proximity to the Thar Desert.
The city’s most prominent landmark is the Jaisalmer Fort, also called Sonar Qila (Golden Fort).

RJS13.claim: Pushkar has the only temple dedicated to Lord Brahma in the world.

evidence.quote: The city of Pushkar is home to the only temple dedicated to Lord Brahma in the whole world.

RJS14.claim: Ranthambore National Park, 14 km from Sawai Madhopur, covers 392 sq km between the Aravallis and Vindhyas and is home to tigers and over 300 bird species.

evidence.quote: Situated 14 km from Sawai Madhopur, the Ranthambore Park gets its name from the Ranthambore Fort situated within its boundaries.
The National Park, situated amidst the Aravalis and Vindhya ranges is spreads over an area of 392 sq.km of thick forest punctuated with pleasant waterfalls.
It is home to the elusive tiger, other animals found here include chinkara, sambhar, cheetal and over 300 species of birds.

RJS15.claim: Ajmer is a pilgrimage centre for Hindus and Muslims; the dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti draws Muslims from around the world.

evidence.quote: Ajmer remains a popular tourist attraction, in addition to being a pilgrimage centre for both Hindus and Muslims.
The final resting place of the Sufi Saint, Khwaja Moinuddin Hasan Chisti, is visited by Muslims from all over the world

RJS16.claim: Mount Abu is Rajasthan's only hill station, at 1,722 metres in the Aravallis.

evidence.quote: Mount Abu, the state’s only hill station stands at a height of 1722 metres above sea level, and is embraced by lush green hills of the Aravalli range.

RJS17.claim: Jodhpur, Rajasthan's second-largest city, is known as the Blue City for its blue-painted buildings.

evidence.quote: Jodhpur, the second largest city in Rajasthan is popularly known as the Blue City.
The name is clearly befitting as most of the architecture – forts, palaces, temples, havelis and even houses are built in vivid shades of blue.

TNS1.claim: Tamil Nadu has four international airports — Chennai, Coimbatore, Tiruchirappalli and Madurai — and domestic airports at Salem and Tuticorin.

evidence.quote: The four international airports in Chennai, Coimbatore, Tiruchirapalli and Madurai serve the main four regions of the state.
The three domestic airports are in Salem, Tuticorin and Puducherry.

TNS2.claim: Tamil Nadu is the home of Southern Railway; Chennai Central handles trains to the north and Chennai Egmore trains to the south.

evidence.quote: The headquarters of Southern Railway is in Tamil Nadu.
Puratchi Thalaivar Dr M.G. Ramachandran Central Railway Station is the gateway to trains towards the north and Chennai Egmore is the hub of trains towards the south.

TNS3.claim: The State Express Transport Corporation (SETC) runs long-distance buses between the main cities, tourist and pilgrim towns, with advance booking.

evidence.quote: The State Express Transport Corporation (SETC) runs long-distance express services and links all important cities, tourist destinations, religious places and commercial hubs
The SETC allows advance booking

TNS4.claim: The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram and the Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram together form the 'Great Living Chola Temples' World Heritage Site.

evidence.quote: Considered as one of the three ‘Great Living Chola Temples’ along with the Gangaikondacholeeswaram Temple and Airavastesvara Temple, the complex is also listed as a part of the UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

TNS5.claim: Madurai can be visited year-round, but December to February is the most comfortable.

evidence.quote: It is a destination that can be visited any time of the year. However, for the best experience, visit the destination during December to February.

places.name: Uttar Pradesh
places.summary: India's most visited state for domestic travellers, home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Varanasi and the newly inscribed Sarnath.
places.seoTitle: Uttar Pradesh Travel Guide: Agra, Varanasi & Sarnath
places.seoDescription: Plan a trip to Uttar Pradesh: the Taj Mahal and Agra's Mughal monuments, Varanasi's ghats and the UNESCO-listed Buddhist site of Sarnath.

images.alt: Boats on the Ganga in front of Dashashwamedh Ghat in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh
images.caption: Dashashwamedh Ghat, Varanasi

overview.text:
Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India and, by the Ministry of Tourism's count, the most visited: it recorded 646.81 million domestic tourist visits in 2024, more than a fifth of the national total, along with 2.27 million foreign tourist visits. Lucknow is the state capital, but most travellers come for two places in particular.

Agra holds three World Heritage Sites — the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri — and the Taj Mahal is the country's most visited ticketed monument for both Indian and foreign visitors. Further east, Varanasi sits on the Ganga, and just outside it the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in July 2026.

Use this page as a starting point: the destination guides below cover each city in detail, with visiting rules, getting there, where to stay and ready-made itineraries.

items.body: Agra and Varanasi are far apart — plan an overnight train or a flight between them rather than a day trip.
Check each monument's weekly closing day before you fix your dates — the destination guides list them.
In the hotter months, plan outdoor sightseeing for early morning and late afternoon.

items.title: Braj (Mathura, Vrindavan, Barsana)
items.body: Krishna's land: temples, ghats on the Yamuna and the most famous Holi in India.

items.title: Agra
items.body: Three World Heritage Sites — the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri.

items.title: Awadh (Lucknow, Ayodhya)
items.body: The Nawabs' capital and its monuments and food; Ayodhya, revered as Rama's birthplace.

items.title: Kashi and the Sangam (Varanasi, Prayagraj)
items.body: The ghats of Varanasi, the Triveni Sangam and the Kumbh and Magh Melas.

items.title: Buddhist sites
items.body: Sarnath, Kushinagar, Kapilvastu and Sravasti.

best_time.text:
October to March is the most comfortable time to travel: Lucknow's winters are cool and dry from late November to February, Mathura is pleasant from October to March, and autumn is the best season in Varanasi. Summer, from late March, is hot, with dry winds called loo; the south-west monsoon then brings most of the rain.

Plan around the festivals too: Prayagraj's Magh Mela (mid-January to mid-February), Lathmar Holi in Barsana (February or March), and Varanasi's Chhath and Bharat Milap.

how_to_reach.text: Fly into the airport nearest your first city: Lucknow's is 14 km from the centre, Varanasi's 22 km and Ayodhya's about 10 km from Ayodhya Dham. The Agra and Purvanchal expressways link Lucknow with Agra and eastern Uttar Pradesh, and the state's cities are well connected by train. Each destination guide below has the details.

items.body: Awadhi biryani, kebabs and nihari in Lucknow.
Dum gosht and other slow-cooked Mughal dishes.
Petha, Agra's famous sweet.
Pedas and kachori in Mathura.
Chikankari embroidery in Lucknow.
Zari and silk in Varanasi.
Metalwork from Moradabad.
Pottery from Khurja and Chunar.

items.title: What are the must-visit places in Uttar Pradesh?
items.body: Agra's Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri; Varanasi's ghats; Lucknow's Imambaras; Mathura and Vrindavan; Ayodhya; Prayagraj's Sangam; and the Buddhist sites at Sarnath and Kushinagar.

items.title: When is the best time to visit Uttar Pradesh?
items.body: October to March, when the weather is cooler. Summers are hot, with loo winds.

items.title: Which festivals are worth planning around?
items.body: The Magh Mela at Prayagraj (mid-January to mid-February) and Lathmar Holi at Barsana (February or March).

items.title: Which airports serve the state?
items.body: Lucknow, Varanasi and Ayodhya are the main ones; each destination guide lists the nearest airport.

places.name: Rajasthan
places.summary: India's largest state: the forts and palaces of Jaipur, Udaipur, Jodhpur and Jaisalmer, the Thar Desert and tiger country at Ranthambore.
places.seoTitle: Rajasthan Travel Guide: Jaipur, Forts, Palaces & Desert
places.seoDescription: Plan a Rajasthan trip: Jaipur's forts and palaces, the UNESCO-listed hill forts, the Thar Desert, wildlife at Ranthambore and Keoladeo, and when to go.

images.commons: File:A bird eye view of Amer Fort Jaipur, India.jpg
images.alt: Aerial view of Amer Fort on its hillside above Maota Lake near Jaipur, Rajasthan
images.caption: Amer Fort above Maota Lake, Jaipur

overview.text:
Rajasthan is India's largest state by area, formed in 1949 from the merger of 22 kingdoms and principalities — which is why it has so many forts and palaces. It recorded 230 million domestic and 2.07 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, fifth among Indian states on both counts.

Its cities are known by colour: Jaipur the pink city, Jodhpur the blue, Udaipur the white and Jaisalmer the golden. Six of its hill forts, including Amber near Jaipur, are together a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Beyond the cities lie the Thar Desert, the bird sanctuary at Keoladeo — another World Heritage Site — and the tiger reserve at Ranthambore.

Most first trips start in Jaipur, the state capital and the third point of the Golden Triangle with Delhi and Agra. The guides below cover each destination in detail.

items.body: Distances are long — plan overnight trains or flights between far-apart cities like Jaipur and Jaisalmer.
In the hot months, plan forts and walking for early morning and late afternoon.
Many forts involve steep climbs and uneven paths — wear sturdy shoes.

items.title: Dhundhar (Jaipur)
items.body: Jaipur's Amber Fort, and Ranthambore's tigers to the south-east.

items.title: Mewar (Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh)
items.body: Lakes and palaces, and two of the great Hill Forts.

items.title: Marwar and the Thar (Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Bikaner)
items.body: The Blue City, the Golden City and the desert dunes.

items.title: Ajmer and Pushkar
items.body: A great Sufi shrine and a holy lake town 14 km apart.

items.title: Mount Abu
items.body: Rajasthan's only hill station.

best_time.text:
Winter — roughly October to January — is the best time for most trips, with mild days of about 10–30°C. It is also festival season: the Jaipur Literature Festival, the Udaipur World Music Festival and the Pushkar Fair all fall in winter, and Jaisalmer's Desert Festival follows around January–February.

Summers are hot and dry, up to 48°C; Mount Abu, Ranakpur and Kumbhalgarh stay pleasant then. The monsoon turns the state green and brings the Teej festival.

how_to_reach.text: Rajasthan's three major airports are Jaipur (international), Jodhpur and Udaipur. Jaipur and Kota are the main rail hubs, with Udaipur, Jodhpur, Ajmer, Bikaner and Abu Road also on the network, and NH-8 between Delhi and Mumbai runs through Jaipur, Ajmer, Udaipur and Chittorgarh. Each destination guide lists its nearest airport and station.

items.title: What is the best time to visit Rajasthan?
items.body: Winter, roughly October to January, when days are mild and the big festivals take place.

items.title: Which forts are World Heritage Sites?
items.body: The Hill Forts of Rajasthan: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer, inscribed together in 2013.

items.title: Which airports serve Rajasthan?
items.body: Jaipur (international), Jodhpur and Udaipur are the main airports.

items.title: When is the Pushkar camel fair?
items.body: For about a week between October and November.

places.name: Maharashtra
places.summary: India's leading state for foreign visitors: Mumbai's heritage and food, the rock-cut caves of Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta, the Konkan coast and the Western Ghats.
places.seoTitle: Maharashtra Travel Guide: Mumbai, Ajanta, Ellora & Konkan
places.seoDescription: Plan a Maharashtra trip: Mumbai's World Heritage architecture and Elephanta Caves, Ajanta and Ellora, the Konkan coast, Western Ghats treks and local food.

images.alt: The Gothic Revival facade and central dome of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai
images.caption: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Mumbai

overview.text:
Maharashtra received more foreign tourist visits than any other Indian state in 2024 — 3.70 million — largely because Mumbai, its capital, is one of India's main international gateways. It is the land where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj founded the Maratha Empire in the 17th century, and its forts and temples still carry that history.

The state's World Heritage Sites span two thousand years: the rock-cut caves of Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta, and in Mumbai, the Gothic Revival Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco ensembles around the Oval Maidan. Beyond the cities, the state runs from the beaches of the Konkan coast up into the Sahyadri ranges of the Western Ghats.

Come hungry: vada pav, misal pav, puran poli and modak are all Maharashtrian classics, and Ganesh Chaturthi is celebrated here with more fervour than anywhere else.

items.body: Avoid the coast and the Ghats at the height of the monsoon if you want easy travel — roads and ferries can be disrupted.
Book trains and hotels early around Ganesh Chaturthi and Diwali.
Ajanta and Ellora are a long way from Mumbai — plan them as a separate leg of the trip rather than a day out.

best_time.text: The cooler months are best: October to February in Pune, and November to March around Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for Ajanta and Ellora.

how_to_reach.text: Fly into Mumbai (BOM) or Nagpur (NAG); Pune and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar are the bases for the Western Ghats and the cave sites.

items.body: See the Kailasa Temple at Ellora and the paintings of Ajanta.
Pay respects at the Shirdi Sai Baba Temple.
Take the Konkan coast: Ganpatipule, Alibaug and Ratnagiri.
Cool off in Mahabaleshwar, a hill station at about 4,500 ft.
See Lonar Lake, formed by a meteor strike about 52,000 years ago.
Vada pav on Mumbai's streets.
A traditional Maharashtrian thali.
Fresh strawberries and shakes in Mahabaleshwar in season.
Ganesh Chaturthi and Diwali are celebrated with great enthusiasm; Gudi Padwa marks the new year.

places.name: Tamil Nadu
places.summary: Temple country of the south: Pallava and Chola monuments, Chennai, the Nilgiri hills and Tamil food, music and dance.
places.seoTitle: Tamil Nadu Travel Guide: Chennai, Temples & Mahabalipuram
places.seoDescription: Plan a Tamil Nadu trip: Chennai, the Pallava monuments of Mahabalipuram, the Great Living Chola Temples, the Nilgiri Mountain Railway, food and festivals.

images.commons: File:Gopurams of Kapaleeshwarar Temple, Mylapore, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India (2012).jpg
images.alt: The carved gopurams of the Kapaleeshwarar Temple in Mylapore, Chennai
images.caption: Kapaleeshwarar Temple, Chennai

overview.text:
Tamil Nadu recorded 306.8 million domestic tourist visits in 2024 — the second most of any state — and 1.16 million foreign visits. It is above all a land of temples: its World Heritage Sites include the Pallava monuments of Mahabalipuram and the Great Living Chola Temples, alongside the Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

Tamil culture is a draw in its own right — Carnatic music, Bharatanatyam dance, and meals served on a banana leaf with sambar and coconut chutney. Pongal, the harvest festival, is the year's great celebration.

Most visitors start in Chennai, the capital, and follow the coast south to Mahabalipuram and on to Puducherry.

items.body: Dress modestly and remove your shoes at temples; some inner sanctums are for Hindus only.
Temple towns get very busy at festival times — book rooms early.

items.title: Chennai and the north coast
items.body: The capital, Pallava Kanchipuram — the 'Golden City of a Thousand Temples' — and Mamallapuram.

items.title: The Chola heartland (Thanjavur)
items.body: The three Great Living Chola Temples on the UNESCO list.

items.title: Madurai and the south
items.body: The Meenakshi temple city, the Char Dham island of Rameswaram and Kanyakumari, India's southern tip.

items.title: The hills
items.body: Ooty, the Queen of Hill Stations, and Kodaikanal, the Princess of Hills.

best_time.text: For the temple towns and the coast, the cooler months are best: December to February for Madurai and Thanjavur, October to February for Kanchipuram, October to March for Rameswaram and November to March for Kanyakumari. Head for the hills when the plains heat up — Ooty is best from March to June and Kodaikanal from April to June.

how_to_reach.text: Tamil Nadu has four international airports — Chennai, Coimbatore, Tiruchirappalli and Madurai — plus domestic airports at Salem and Tuticorin. Southern Railway is headquartered here, with Chennai Central for trains north and Chennai Egmore for trains south, and major junctions at Madurai, Coimbatore, Tiruchirappalli and Nagercoil. The state's SETC runs long-distance buses with advance booking.

items.title: What is the best time to visit Tamil Nadu?
items.body: About October to March for the plains and coast; March to June for Ooty and Kodaikanal.

items.title: Which international airports serve Tamil Nadu?
items.body: Chennai, Coimbatore, Tiruchirappalli and Madurai.

items.title: What are the Great Living Chola Temples?
items.body: The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram and the Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram, listed together by UNESCO.

places.name: Bihar
places.summary: The land of the Buddha: Bodh Gaya, Rajgir and Nalanda, the birthplace of Buddhism and Jainism, Madhubani art and the Chhath festival.
places.seoTitle: Bihar Travel Guide: Bodh Gaya, Nalanda & Rajgir
places.seoDescription: Plan a Bihar trip: Bodh Gaya's Mahabodhi Temple, the ruins of Nalanda, Rajgir's sacred hills, Madhubani art, Chhath and the best time to visit.

images.alt: The tall carved spire of the Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya
images.caption: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya

overview.text:
Bihar takes its name from 'vihara', a Buddhist monastery, and it is the birthplace of both Buddhism and Jainism. The Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, taught on the hills of Rajgir, and Nalanda grew into one of the ancient world's great universities. Foreign tourist visits reached 0.737 million in 2024, up 35% on the year before.

Patna, the state capital, was once Pataliputra, and its Takhat Sri Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, is revered by Sikhs. Bihar's living culture is just as distinctive: Madhubani painting, made by women of the Mithila region, and Chhath, the festival to the Sun God, usually between late October and mid-November.

items.body: The Buddhist sites are spread out — hire a car and driver to link them.
Book rooms early in winter, the main pilgrimage season.
Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Guru Gobind Singh's birthplace.
The Bihar Museum in Patna.

places.seoTitle: West Bengal Travel Guide: Kolkata, Darjeeling & Sundarbans
places.seoDescription: Plan a West Bengal trip: Kolkata's museums and Durga Puja, the Sundarbans, Bishnupur's terracotta temples, Darjeeling's toy train and Bengali sweets.

images.alt: The white marble Victoria Memorial in Kolkata with its central dome and gardens
images.caption: Victoria Memorial, Kolkata

overview.text:
West Bengal runs from the Bay of Bengal to the Himalaya. Kolkata, its capital, is known as India's cultural capital and is home to the Indian Museum, founded in 1814, and the Victoria Memorial; Bishnupur has terracotta temples, and the Sundarbans mangrove forest is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the north lie the tea gardens of Darjeeling.

The state's grandest festival is Durga Puja, celebrated over nine days with elaborate pandals, and Bengali food — from hilsa to rasogolla and sandesh — is a highlight of any trip. West Bengal received 3.12 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, second among Indian states.

places.seoDescription: Plan a Punjab trip: Amritsar's Golden Temple and Jallianwala Bagh, Virasat-e-Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib, Patiala's Qila Mubarak and the Harike wetland.

images.commons: File:Golden Temple or Harmandir Sahib - AMRITSAR.JPG
images.alt: The gilded Harmandir Sahib reflected in the Amrit Sarovar pool, Amritsar, under a cloudy sky
images.caption: The Golden Temple, Amritsar

overview.text:
Punjab is the heartland of Sikhism. In Amritsar, the Golden Temple is the faith's spiritual centre, where the langar serves free meals to all, and nearby Jallianwala Bagh recalls the massacre of 1919. At Anandpur Sahib, Virasat-e-Khalsa tells the story of the Sikh community, and the town hosts Hola Mohalla, a festival of martial arts and culture.

Beyond the Sikh sites, Patiala's Qila Mubarak and Kapurthala's mirrored Sheesh Mahal, inspired by Versailles, recall the state's royal past, and Harike Wetland, where the Beas and Sutlej meet, is the largest wetland in northern India. Punjab recorded 27.7 million domestic and 0.54 million foreign tourist visits in 2024.

places.seoTitle: Jammu and Kashmir Travel Guide & Current Advisories
places.seoDescription: Jammu and Kashmir: Srinagar's Dal Lake and Mughal gardens, Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Amarnath and Vaishno Devi, Kashmiri food — and the travel advisories to check first.

images.alt: Boatmen paddling across a still Dal Lake below snow-covered mountains
images.caption: Dal Lake, Srinagar

overview.text:
Jammu and Kashmir recorded 23.0 million domestic and 0.065 million foreign tourist visits in 2024. Its houseboats on the Dal and Nigeen lakes, spring tulips and mountain resorts draw visitors to the Kashmir Valley, while the Amarnath cave and the Vaishno Devi Temple draw pilgrims from across India. In Jammu, try khatta meat, madra and khameera bread.

Check current travel advice before planning a trip. As of October 2026, the UK government advises against all travel to the Union Territory, including Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg, except air travel to and within Jammu city. On 22 April 2025, militants killed 26 civilians, most of them tourists, near Pahalgam.
